intro: Sport runs on categories and on public support. A governing body decides who may enter the women's race, which Paralympic class an athlete belongs in, and what evidence settles a dispute. A city council or state legislature decides whether taxes pay for a stadium and whether homes can be taken to clear land for it.

This unit follows both kinds of decision through real cases. You will read about the Women's World Games of 1922, chromosome tests from 1968, the Semenya and Pistorius cases at the Court of Arbitration for Sport, and the Sydney 2000 ban. You will also trace Soldier Field, the Illinois Sports Facilities Authority, Chavez Ravine, the Colts' move and the tax code.

By the end you will be able to name who wrote a rule, what evidence it used, who it let in or shut out, and which court or vote tested it. You will also be able to weigh a public stadium deal using what economists measured, and build an argument from dated records instead of slogans.
bigQuestion: Who gets to decide which bodies count in sport and how much the public pays for it, and how can those decisions be challenged?

timeline.t: The FSFI holds the first Women's World Games in Paris
Chicago's lakefront stadium, later Soldier Field, opens
Los Angeles voters approve the Dodgers' Chavez Ravine contract
Congress lists pro football leagues under a tax exemption
The IOC begins chromosome testing of women athletes
The Colts move from Baltimore to Indianapolis overnight
Illinois creates the Illinois Sports Facilities Authority
The IOC votes to end routine sex screening before Sydney
A fraud at the Sydney Paralympics leads to an IPC suspension
The Supreme Court decides Kelo v. City of New London
CAS overturns the IAAF ban on Oscar Pistorius
The IOC hands eligibility rules to each sport's federation

test.q: Why did Alice Milliat's FSFI hold the Women's World Games?
choices: The IOC refused women's track events
test.why: The FSFI built a parallel meet when the IOC refused women's track.

test.q: When did women first compete in Olympic track and field?
test.why: Five women's track events appeared at Amsterdam in 1928.

test.q: What did the Barr body test examine?
choices: Cheek cells for a chromosome marker
test.why: The IOC's 1968 test looked at cheek cells for two X chromosomes.

test.q: What changed when the IOC ended routine sex screening before 2000?
test.why: Officials could still review a questioned athlete, but not everyone.

test.q: What did CAS rule in the Dutee Chand case in 2015?
choices: The IAAF had not shown enough evidence, so its rules were suspended
India must hold its own games
test.why: The panel suspended the hyperandrogenism rules for lack of evidence.

test.q: Why did the IPC suspend intellectual impairment events after 2000?
choices: A Spanish team was found to have players without impairments
The events moved to the Olympics
test.why: The Sydney basketball fraud led the IPC to suspend those events.

test.q: What principle decided the Pistorius case at CAS in 2008?
choices: The governing body had to prove an advantage
Olympic rules do not apply to relays
test.why: CAS said the IAAF had not proven the prosthetics gave an overall advantage.

test.q: Since 2021, who writes transgender eligibility rules in Olympic sport?
test.why: The IOC's 2021 framework left the rules to each federation.

test.q: Who built the stadium that opened on Chicago's lakefront in 1924?
test.why: A public park board built what became Soldier Field.

test.q: What did the Illinois Sports Facilities Authority first build?
choices: A new park for the White Sox
test.why: The ISFA was created in 1987 and built New Comiskey Park, opened in 1991.

test.q: What happened to the land at Chavez Ravine after its housing plan was canceled?
choices: The city offered it to the Dodgers
test.why: In 1957 the city offered the cleared land to the Dodgers, and voters approved in 1958.

test.q: What does the Fifth Amendment require when government takes property?
test.why: The takings clause requires public use and just compensation.

test.q: Why did the Colts leave Baltimore at night in March 1984?
choices: Maryland was moving to seize the team by eminent domain
test.why: The owner moved before Maryland's eminent domain law could be used.

test.q: What did Noll and Zimbalist's 1997 study conclude about stadiums?
choices: They showed little effect on local growth
test.why: Their collected studies found few if any positive local effects.

test.q: How does the American path to pro sport differ from European club academies?
choices: American public schools bear training costs and receive nothing later
test.why: US schools pay with taxes, while European clubs train players and receive compensation.

write.prompt: Pick one question: Should sports bodies or courts have the final word on who fits a category? Or should a city pay for a stadium a private team uses? Argue your answer using at least three dated records from this unit, such as the 2008 Pistorius ruling, the 2015 Chand ruling, the 1958 Chavez Ravine referendum or the 1997 Noll and Zimbalist study. Explain what each record says.
tips: Name each record and its year.
Say who wrote each rule or made each decision.
Describe both sides before you choose one.
Use terms from the unit, such as eligibility, burden of proof and eminent domain.
Describe people with care and use the words they use for themselves.
